findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Name the specific document the printed copy refers to (e.g., "a printed copy of the budget summary").
findings.violation: "A printed copy" has no clear antecedent - it's unclear whether this refers to the budget, the policy, or some other document.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the people operations office updates the equipment catalog each quarter."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a transition that doesn't imply false parallelism, or move this sentence to its own unconnected point.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies a parallel to the prior sentence about requesting printed copies, but updating a catalog quarterly is not similar to that action; the connector doesn't logically link the two ideas.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Explicitly state which eligibility timer ("the 90-day service requirement" or "the benefit-year claim window") resumes on return.
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is never defined - it's unclear whether this refers to the 90-day service requirement, the once-per-benefit-year claim window, or something else.

findings.evidence: "eligibility for the workspace stipend depends on several details"
findings.fix: Use one consistent name for the stipend throughout the document.
findings.violation: The document is titled "Home-Office Equipment Stipend Policy" and otherwise refers to "the stipend," but this paragraph suddenly calls it "the workspace stipend," suggesting an inconsistently named or possibly different benefit.

findings.evidence: "A workspace used only occasionally for calls does not meet the bar the stipend policy sets."
findings.fix: Define the specific usage threshold that qualifies a workspace (e.g., "used as the primary work location at least X days per week").
findings.violation: "The bar" is never quantified or defined (e.g., hours per week, primary vs. occasional use), making this criterion unenforceable.

findings.evidence: "The reviewer logs every workspace confirmation in the same shared tracking sheet the benefits team maintains."
findings.fix: Introduce the tracking sheet before referring back to it, or remove "same."
findings.violation: "The same shared tracking sheet" implies a previously mentioned tracking sheet, but no tracking sheet has been introduced anywhere earlier in the document.

findings.evidence: "A workspace confirmation from more than one year ago no longer satisfies the stipend requirement on its own."
findings.fix: Define "benefit year" once and use that defined term consistently instead of switching to "one year."
findings.violation: The document uses "benefit year" elsewhere as the operative time unit but never defines it (fiscal year? anniversary year?), and here switches to a rolling "one year," so it's unclear if these are the same period.

findings.evidence: "Employees must submit the receipt, the manager's approval form, and the original purchase order before the review begins."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two sections so they state the same documentation requirements.
findings.violation: This requires an "original purchase order" for review, but the Required Documentation section later says "a photo of the receipt is enough for most requests," directly conflicting on what documentation is actually required.

findings.evidence: "Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Clarify the actual order of steps (e.g., "reviews a draft summary before submitting" or "reviews the confirmation after submitting").
findings.violation: The sequence is illogical - a "confirmation summary" implies something generated after submission, yet the text says the employee reviews it before submitting.

findings.evidence: "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Use consistent units (business days) for both figures and clarify how the reminder relates to the two-day review window.
findings.violation: The manager's review window is stated as "two business days" while the reminder trigger is "three days" with no unit specified (business or calendar), leaving the actual timeline internally inconsistent.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: List the specific request types that require more than a photo receipt.
findings.violation: "Most requests" implies exceptions exist but never specifies what those exceptions are or what additional documentation they require.

findings.evidence: "The finance office conducts an evaluation of every submitted receipt before it approves the amount."
findings.fix: Add the actual stipend amount(s) or reference the specific document/table that lists them.
findings.violation: The section is titled "Reimbursement Amounts" but never actually states any dollar amount, cap, or per-category limit for the stipend.

findings.evidence: "this office may ask for a brief photo check once a year"
findings.fix: Name the specific office responsible for the photo check.
findings.violation: "This office" has no clear antecedent - the preceding sentence refers to "the applicant," not any office, so it's unclear which of the several offices mentioned elsewhere (benefits, finance, people operations) is meant.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee whenever the benefits team confirms that the role genuinely requires a second device"
findings.fix: Split into separate sentences: state the one-device-per-category default rule, then separately state the fieldwork exception permitting a second device.
findings.violation: This sentence contradicts itself, stating a "one device per category" limit while simultaneously describing conditions under which "a second device" is allowed, all packed into a single unreadable run-on clause.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form."
findings.fix: Rewrite this section in third person to match the rest of the document.
findings.violation: This section switches to second-person "you" while every other section uses third person ("the employee," "the applicant"), an inconsistent point of view.

findings.evidence: "Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Use one consistently named tracking artifact throughout, or explain how the request log and tracking sheet relate.
findings.violation: A new artifact, "the request log," is introduced here without clarifying whether it's the same as "the shared tracking sheet" mentioned in the Eligibility section, creating ambiguity about how many tracking systems exist.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either list the complete set of steps here or remove this section and rely on "How to Apply."
findings.violation: This section claims to describe the request steps but lists only two, omitting the manager approval form, purchase order, and confirmation summary review steps already described in "How to Apply," making the two sections inconsistent.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison reviews the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Assign budget review/tracking to a single, consistently named owner across the document.
findings.violation: This contradicts Program Overview, which states "The benefits team tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year" - two different parties are assigned the same task.

findings.evidence: "The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the approver is always the employee's manager or varies by department, and use consistent language.
findings.violation: This implies the approver varies by department, but the Approval Timeline section consistently refers to "the manager" as the sole approver, creating an inconsistency about who approves requests.

findings.evidence: "The escalation of repeat requests happens automatically within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Define what constitutes a "repeat request" and describe what the escalation process actually entails.
findings.violation: "Repeat requests" and the escalation process are never defined or explained anywhere else in the document, so this requirement is unenforceable as written.

findings.evidence: "The people operations office tracks the stipend budget at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicated/misapplied sentence and settle on one consistent owner for stipend budget tracking.
findings.violation: This is a near copy of the Program Overview's sentence about the equipment catalog, but here it's misapplied to budget tracking (which doesn't have "entries" in the way a catalog does) and names a third different owner (people operations office) for the same budget task already attributed to the benefits team and the finance liaison elsewhere.
